title: Joe Gabriel's Thibodaux brass and dance band
summary: Joe Gabriel, a violinist, led a brass band and an eight-piece dance orchestra sounding like the Piron band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Did they have a brass band up there that never had many parades or anything right in Thibodeau that you remember when you were a kid?
Well, yeah, Joe Gabriel. And he had orchestra.
Yeah, I mean, I wondered about the brass band.

Well, he was a violin player and when they had a Kishens or brass band, well, they would form into a brass band. Joe Gabriel would lead the band like a band major. He was a violin player. He didn't play no other instrument, but he would direct them and they would play brass bands.

Can you remember what any of the dance bands were like up there when you were, oh, as far back as you can remember? That is, did it sound like the New Orleans jazz bands here? Was it a different type of music? What would you say? How did it compare?
Well, their band sounded, the orchestra, like old Pierron band.
Oh, yes. Yeah. They made a few records, so we have an idea about how that sounded.
Yeah, well, that's right. He had a band, something on the order.
That's right, that's right. That's the kind of band.
About how big was the dance band, if you can remember when you'd hear it?
About the same size as the ones here.
Yeah, that's right. They had about eight pieces.
